The evidence strongly supports this claim:
1. E1 explicitly states "Our effective tax rate in 2025 increased compared to 2024, mostly due to the effects of OBBBA" (One Big Beautiful Bill Act - U.S. tax law)
2. Multiple evidence passages (E1, E2, E3) confirm a $15.93 billion one-time charge was recorded in Q3 2025 related to OBBBA implementation
3. E4 reiterates that the effective tax rate increase was "mostly due to the implementation of OBBBA"

The evidence directly establishes both components of the claim: (1) the effective tax rate increased in 2025, and (2) this increase was mainly caused by a one-time charge related to U.S. tax law changes (OBBBA). The filing explicitly attributes the causation, which is required for interpretive claims.

After investigating potential challenges to the initial verdict, all three hypotheses were refuted by the evidence:

H1 (Full year vs Q3 only): CHALLENGE_REFUTED. E14 from the 10-K explicitly shows the effective tax rate for the full year ended December 31, 2025 was 30% compared to 12% in 2024, confirming the rate increased for the full year, not just Q3. E1 also explicitly states "Our effective tax rate in 2025 increased compared to 2024, mostly due to the effects of OBBBA" referring to the full year.

H2 (Other significant factors): CHALLENGE_REFUTED. E1 explicitly states the increase was "mostly due to the effects of OBBBA," establishing OBBBA as the main cause. E11 shows the tax rate reconciliation for 2024 and 2023, where other factors like share-based compensation, R&D credits, and foreign-derived intangible income deduction had relatively consistent impacts across years and were rate-reducing factors, not rate-increasing ones that would explain the 2025 increase.

H3 (Discrete item excluded from rate): CHALLENGE_REFUTED. While E13 describes the charge as a "discrete charge," E14 clearly shows the effective tax rate of 30% for 2025 includes this charge (compared to 12% in 2024). The charge was included in the provision for income taxes and the effective tax rate calculation, not excluded from it.

The verdict remains SUPPORTED. The evidence confirms both that the effective tax rate increased in 2025 (from 12% to 30%) and that this increase was mainly caused by the one-time OBBBA charge, as explicitly stated in the filings.

e Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) was enacted, introducing several significant U.S. income tax provisions that will reduce our U.S. federal cash tax payments for the remainder of 2025 and future years. The provisions include the immediate expensing of domestic research and development costs and certain capital expenditures beginning in 2025, as well as an enhanced deduction for foreign-derived intangible income effective in 2026. The benefits from these provisions are limited by the 15% Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax (CAMT). As a result, we recorded a $15.93 billion one-time charge related to the implementation as of the enactment date of OBBBA, including recognition of a valuation allowance against our U.S. federal deferred tax assets. In determining the valuation allowance, our accounting policy incorporates the expected impact of future years’ CAMT in assessing the realizability of our deferred tax assets .
